newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: NWE oil products firm, fuel oil gains late.
newsitem.headline: NWE oil products firm, fuel oil gains late.

text.p: NWE oil products were firmer on Thursday morning, with fuel oil steady until a $2 surge late in the morning, dealers said.

High sulphur fuel oil barges were at a standoff at levels unchanged from Wednesday, $83/$84 fob Rotterdam, until a major bought 3,000 tonnes at $85 fob and offers moved to $86. The strength coincided with growing bunker demand, traders said.
One trader talked of demand reaching 40,000-50,000 tonnes.
"We do have a long weekend coming up in Europe and (shipowners) have been holding off," another trader said.

Gasoline was about $1 a tonne firmer by late morning at $201 offered for delivery Amsterdam-Rotterdam and a further $1/$2 higher for Rotterdam product. Earlier, a eurograde barge traded at $203.50 fob Rotterdam, although the delivery period, to June 5, made it a slightly irregular deal, according to some.

Heating oil barges were very slightly higher by late morning, having shed most of their early $2 gains. Offers for Rotterdam product remained at around IPE June +$1.50 fob Rotterdam, or 75 cents/+$1 fob Antwerp.
Some talked of improved demand from traders, rather than end-consumers, as buying appeared more profitable than producing 0.2 percent sulphur heating oil.
"There's not much sense producing marginal quantities of 0.2 material," one trader said.
